classification.difficultyReason: The supplied diagram and part a scaffold finding the shared height. Part b requires recognising the larger triangle's adjacent side as x+10, reusing the unrounded height in a tangent equation and subtracting the known segment.

spec.description: Two nested right triangles with a collinear horizontal baseline and shared vertical right-hand height. Separate dimension arrows label the left baseline segment x m, the right segment 10 m and the height h m. No vertex names are printed.
spec.mathematics: The smaller triangle has adjacent side 10 m, opposite side h m and angle 31 degrees. The larger triangle has adjacent side (x+10) m, opposite side h m and angle 21 degrees. Both have the right angle at the baseline's right endpoint. Construction coordinates follow these relationships and are not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only printed givens and unknown labels are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the height $h$, correct to the nearest centimetre.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the value of $x$, correct to the nearest centimetre.

answer.short:
$x=5.65\text{ m}$

Use tangent in the larger triangle, then subtract $10\text{ m}$.
answer.worked:
Use the unrounded height $h=10\tan31^{\circ}$ in the larger right triangle.
$$\begin{align*}
\tan21^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{x+10}\\
(x+10)\tan21^{\circ}&=h\\
x+10&=\frac{h}{\tan21^{\circ}}\\
x&=\frac{10\tan31^{\circ}}{\tan21^{\circ}}-10\\
x&\approx5.65\text{ m}
\end{align*}$$
